root.note: No theory is accepted by all dictionaries. Treccani and Wiktionary list several, among them a Lombard word for ‘mouthful’, Latin pinsa and Byzantine Greek pitta.

history: Nobody knows exactly where the word pizza comes from. The first written form is pizze in a document of the year 997 from Gaeta, a town between Rome and Naples. A famous theory links it with a Germanic or Lombard word for a ‘bite’ or ‘mouthful’. Others link it with Latin pinsa, a form of pinsere, ‘to pound’, as in pounding dough, and some with Byzantine Greek pitta, a flat bread. The matter is open, so careful books say ‘of uncertain origin’. The dish itself became famous in Naples, and in the 1900s the word travelled around the world with Italian emigrants. In Italy a pizzeria is the place, and a pizza al taglio is a rectangular one sold by the slice.
historyEinfach: The origin of pizza is not known for sure. The first written form is from the year 997. There are three main ideas: a Germanic word for ‘bite’, Latin pinsa, or Greek pitta. The world learned the word from Italian emigrants.

elsewhere.text: English took the word in the early 20th century, when Italian-American restaurants made the dish well known.
